Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:22590

Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 547 of 2024

Applicant :- Arun Singh @ Arun Kumar And 2 Others
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Farooq Ayoob,Km. Pooja Tiwari Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.Shri Akhand Pratap Singh has filed his power/ Vakalatnama on behalf of the complainant/
informant and the same is taken on record.
2. Learned AGA informs that he has procured complete instructions in the matter including upto date case diary and the investigation of the case is going on.

3. Heard Shri Vivek Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Akhand Pratap Singh,
learned counsel appearing for complainant/ informant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
4.

The present anticipatory bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant - Arun Singh @ Arun Kumar, Shiv Shankar Singh and Shivam Singh in Case Crime No. 34 of 2024, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 342, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station Kotwali Haidergarh, District Arun Singh @ Arun Kumar And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

1 Barabanki, with the prayer to grant them anticipatory bail as they are apprehending arrest in the above-mentioned case.
5.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that it is a case of false implication.

The applicants were not named in the FIR and they have been made accused in this case only on account of their relationship with the accused persons i.e. Rama Devi (their mother) in whose favour a registered Will is made by the deceased Ashok Kumar Singh on 1.11.2023.
6.

It is vehemently submitted that the Will which has been voluntarily made by Ashok Kumar Singh has been duly registered in the Registrar Office and the same may not be termed to have been executed under any duress or confinement as the Ashok Kumar Singh at the time of registration of the Will was present before the Registrar/ Sub Registrar and it is only after his acknowledgment the Will could have been registered.
7.

It is vehemently submitted that one Aditya Pratap Singh is claiming himself to be the son of Ashok Kumar Singh, however, his claim is disputed and in presence of registered Will the same is yet to be adjudicated by a Competent Criminal Court and for that purpose a civil suit appears to have been filed on behalf of Aditya Pratap Singh by his next friend i.e. Ranjit Singh and is pending in the civil court.

8. It is also submitted that the applicants undertake to cooperate in the investigation and would remain present before the Investigating Officer as and when their presence would be required and there is no apprehension that the accused-applicant after release on anticipatory bail, may flee from the process of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

9. Learned AGA as well as Shri Akhand Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the complainant/
informant, vehemently opposes the prayer of anticipatory bail of the applicant on the ground that the Will has been executed after confining Ashok Kumar Singh in detention and the same has not been made with free wish and will.

It is also submitted there is no occasion as to why Shri Ashok Kumar Singh will execute a Will in favour of the mother of the applicants when he is already having a son, namely, Aditya Pratap Singh aged about 10 years, thus the Will has been executed by confining the executor and under duress.

10. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that allegations and counter allegations have been levelled with regard to the execution of a 'Will' by Ashok Kumar Singh in favour of mother of the applicant.

Perusal of a copy of 'Will' which has been placed as Annexure No.2 of the paper book would reveal that same is a registered document and has been registered after acknowledgement of the contents of the same by the maker of the Will, namely,
Ashok Kumar Singh.

The authenticity and legality of this Will is to be adjudicated by the Civil Court in an appropriate proceeding which is shown to have been instituted by the alleged son of the executor of the Will, namely, Aditya Praap Singh as a Civil Suit alleged to have been filed by him.
The dispute appears to be of a civil in nature.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus, the anticipatory bail application moved on behalf of the applicant is disposed of with a direction that till the submission of police report under Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C., in the event of arrest of applicants- Arun Singh @ Arun Kumar, Shiv Shankar Singh and Shivam Singh in the above noted case, they shall be released forthwith on anticipatory bail on their furnishing personal bond of Rs.
50,000/- with two sureties of like amount to the satisfaction of Station House Officer of police station/court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicants shall make themselves available for interrogation by the police officer as and when required, if investigation is in progress;
(ii) The applicants shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade such person from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
(iii) The applicants shall not leave the country without the previous permission of the Court and if they have passport, the same shall be deposited by them before the S.S.P./S.P. concerned/Court concerned.
10.
In default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer / Government Advocate is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of interim anticipatory bail granted to the applicants.
11. The Investigating Officer will continue with the investigation, if it is in progress and the same will not be affected by this order.
